name: 30chars
tagline: A focused writing tool for copy that has to fit inside a hard character limit, like store titles, meta tags and ad headlines.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a counter with taste: text in, live character count out, plus a preview of what gets truncated. None of that requires a server, an account, or anyone else's data. An agent can produce a local single-page app with per-format limits, grapheme-aware counting, side-by-side variants and saved drafts in one sitting, and the counting logic is the boring part that is easy to get right. If the paid version leans on AI rewrite suggestions, you can wire that to your own API key and pay per token instead of per month. What you will not reproduce for free is the sense that someone already thought about which limits matter.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you draft copy against a chosen character limit and see live counts, truncation previews and variant comparisons.
requirements: optional: an LLM API key in .env if you want rewrite suggestions
whatYouLose: A maintained list of current platform limits, which quietly change
Polish: keyboard flow, mobile layout, the small stuff that makes a utility pleasant
Any AI rewrite suggestions that were tuned for tight limits rather than generic prompting
Shared drafts and history across devices unless you add sync yourself
Someone else caring when Unicode, emoji or CJK counting breaks
moatNotes: The defensibility here is interaction design and up to date limit presets, not technology.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because it is cheap relative to the annoyance it removes, and because paying means never thinking about whether the App Store name limit is 30 or 50 characters this year. Tiny single-purpose tools sell convenience and correctness, not capability. If you write constrained copy once a quarter, a local build is fine; if you ship it weekly, the hosted version disappears into your workflow and stays out of your way.
notes: Character counting is a solved problem; the product is the packaging around it.
prompt:
Build a local, single-page web app called "charfit" for writing copy that must fit inside hard character limits.

Stack, no substitutions: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tailwind for styling, Zustand for state, no backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no analytics.

Core behavior:
- A large textarea for the draft, plus a limit selector.
- Built-in presets defined in a single editable src/limits.ts file: App Store app name (30), App Store subtitle (30), Google Play title (30), Google ad headline (30), Google ad description (90), SEO meta title (60), SEO meta description (155), X post (280), YouTube title (100). Each preset has a name, limit, and a short note.
- Allow a custom limit.
- Live counters: characters used, characters remaining, and a colored bar that turns amber at 90 percent and red past the limit.
- Count by grapheme clusters using Intl.Segmenter so emoji and combining marks count as one, and show the naive UTF-16 length as a secondary number since some platforms use it.
- Truncation preview: show exactly what the string looks like cut at the limit, with an ellipsis variant.
- Variants panel: keep up to 8 alternative drafts for the same limit side by side, each with its own counter, with buttons to duplicate, delete and mark one as chosen.
- Persist everything to localStorage under one key, autosaving with a debounce.
- Export the current project as CSV and JSON. Import JSON back.
- Keyboard: cmd/ctrl+enter duplicates the current variant, cmd/ctrl+s exports JSON.

Optional AI rewrites, off by default:
- If VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY is set in .env, show a "tighten" button that asks for 5 rewrites under the current limit and inserts them as variants. Read the key from .env only, never hardcode it, and include .env in .gitignore with a .env.example. If the key is missing, hide the button entirely and never show an error toast about it.

Out of scope: user accounts, cloud sync, teams, payments, a database, server-side rendering.

Deliver: working app on npm run dev, a README with setup in under 10 lines, and unit tests for the grapheme counter and the truncation function using Vitest.
